articles.title: Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats
articles.summary: Planes in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy have been checked for explosives following separate threats.
articles.byline: Emer Moreau, Jaroslav Lukiv, Laura Gozzi

blocks.text: Seven passenger planes across Europe, two of which departed from the UK, have been inspected following a series of suspected bomb threats.

Two Ryanair flights, one originating from Dublin and the other from Lisbon, were searched after landing in Rome following anonymous tips but no explosives were found, sources at the city's Fiumicino airport told the BBC.
The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air Force until landing. Authorities have also searched planes in Poland, Spain and Bulgaria.
While officially there is no link between them, authorities from various countries will be co-operating to assess whether this was a co-ordinated attack, designed to disrupt airspace.
The UK government described today's incidents as "malicious hoax threats".

In a statement it said it had "one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we've seen today".
Aviation security expert Paul Mason said bomb threats on passenger planes "don't happen that frequently", which made the latest incidents "unusual".

"It sounds like they've been made in a credible manner across a broad range of airlines," Mason told BBC Radio 5 Live. "That would suggest to me that it's been a very deliberate act by a typical actor rather than a load of coincidental, malicious calls."
He said "there are a lot of processes" that the onboard crew and people on the ground must go through "to validate the credibility of the threat".

A flight may be asked to divert if the credibility of a threat "is of a certain level", Mason added, and in some cases the onboard crew may not even be advised on what the ground operators were dealing with.
In Rome, sources at Fiumicino airport told the BBC police bomb disposal experts carried out standard security protocols to ensure the safety of all passengers and crew.
Inspections of the passengers, luggage, and the aircraft yielded negative results, and the alert has since been cleared.
One plane which landed in Murcia, southern Spain - a Ryanair flight coming from Manchester - was also found not to have any explosives on board, Spanish authorities said.
One passenger later said she was unaware of the bomb threat until after the plane landed.
"We weren't told anything during the flight," Sarah told BBC Radio 5 Live. "The plane stopped quite suddenly and then we were kept on the runway for around 30 minutes."
"Then the fire engines turned up, the bomb squad turned up and we were asked to evacuate," she continues.

Sarah said the plane had not been on the ground a minute before it was "surrounded by fire engines and police and a bomb squad". All the passengers were then escorted by police, leaving all their belongings.
"We were only later told that it was an actual threat, a bomb threat to the plane itself," she added.
Two flights heading to Warsaw were also affected, including one from London Heathrow.
The Heathrow flight was originally meant to land at the Polish capital's main airport, Chopin, but was diverted instead to the smaller Modlin airport, briefly forcing its closure.
A Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen to Warsaw-Chopin landed as planned.
Later on Tuesday, Bulgarian Transport Minister Georgi Peev said there were bomb threats against two planes travelling to the country's capital Sofia.
He told the state-owned Bulgarian News Agency (BTA) the flights were from the northern Italian city of Bergamo and Ireland's capital Dublin.
The flights into Sofia were not diverted and no explosives were found when the planes were checked, Peev said.

Bulgaria's border police said in a statement sent to the BBC that at around 10:35 (08:35 GMT) it had received an email about "the presence of an improvised explosive device on a flight returning from Bergamo".
"Standard procedures for such incidents were immediately activated, and an operational headquarters comprising representatives of various institutions was convened," the statement said.
The border police added that the same email also reported a "similar threat against aircraft arriving from Dublin".
These incidents come a day after a Wizz Air flight from London Luton made an emergency landing in Budapest, escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet, after a bomb threat.
Wizz Air said later that security checks had been made and nothing was found.
BBC Verify has consulted aviation safety experts about what happens on board a plane when a bomb threat is issued.

Marco Chan, a former pilot for Cathay Pacific Airways and Hong Kong Airlines who is now a senior lecturer in aviation operations at Kingston University, said a bomb threat is considered "genuine until it is resolved, even though most turn out to be hoaxes".

Chan said crews will "quietly search" toilets, galleys and storage areas and will not touch a suspicious item unless it has to be taken to an area on the aircraft designated as the least risky bomb location.
The aircraft's captain will have multiple factors to assess, according to former airline pilot Terry Tozer, an aviation safety commentator.
He said these include what facilities are available at the airport they are being diverted to and how the plane can continue onwards should it turn out to be a false threat.
Chan added that once on the ground, the plane is generally "taken to an isolated stand, passengers are disembarked, and police and bomb disposal teams search it".

articles.title: US man charged with mailing hundreds of letters containing powder to officials before midterms
articles.summary:
Oklahoma man accused of sending letters with white nonhazardous powder before 2024 and 2026 elections

Federal authorities have charged an Oklahoma man with sending hundreds of letters…

blocks.text: Federal authorities have charged an Oklahoma man with sending hundreds of letters containing nonhazardous white powder to public officials before the 2024 and 2026 elections.
The powders turned out to be yeast or flour, though not all letters have been fully tested, the FBI said in a court filing made public Tuesday.

Robin Martin is charged with conveying a hoax and mailing threatening communications. Martin was expected to make his initial court appearance Tuesday afternoon in Oklahoma City. Online records do not list an attorney to comment on his behalf.

Federal authorities announced last month that they were investigating letters with “suspicious substances” that had been mailed to congressional and election offices nationwide and urged recipients to treat the mailings as “potentially hazardous”.

A message from the Senate sergeant at arms obtained by the Associated Press said law enforcement officials were working to intercept any additional letters, but “it is possible that some letters may reach their destinations.”

The FBI said at the time that the bureau and the Postal Inspection Service were investigating. The FBI referred questions to the US attorney’s office Tuesday, and the Postal Inspection Service didn’t immediately return an email message from the AP seeking comment.

articles.title: UK makes huge aid cuts to Commonwealth nations despite warm words at Chogm summit
articles.summary:
Nations in the group fare worse than others, with funding for nature projects especially hard hit even as climate crisis intensifies global need

The UK government has slashed overseas aid to…

blocks.text: The UK government has slashed overseas aid to Commonwealth countries, the Guardian can reveal, in contrast to the warm words for the group from King Charles and the prime minister, Andy Burnham, this week.
Amid sharp cuts in the UK’s aid budget overall, the Commonwealth has fared poorly, an analysis of the most recent and projected aid figures, seen by the Guardian, has shown.

Funding from the UK to the Commonwealth nations that previously had bilateral aid programmes will be cut from £546m in 2024-25 to £131m in 2028-29. Of that total, a large chunk – £68m – will go to Nigeria, leaving £63m for other countries.

The revelations come as the king attends the Commonwealth heads of government meeting (Chogm) this week in Antigua, where he said it was “only right that we should acknowledge the great suffering and injustices” of slavery but where Burnham’s government fought to ensure that any discussion of reparations would be off the agenda.

The government has been cutting back on aid to countries that have been rapidly developing and are now judged to be middle income, such as India and Antigua, but the cuts to Commonwealth countries go much further, including many countries that are still among the poorest and many that are struggling under heavy debt burdens.

For example, Sierra Leone, one of the world’s least developed countries, will have its aid slashed from nearly £30m in 2024-25 to £5m in 2028-29. The UK and Sierra Leone will act as co-conveners of a strand of talks focusing on adaptation to the impacts of the climate crisis, at the Cop31 climate summit in Turkey next week.

Aid to Rwanda, where the previous government had a scheme to send refugees, is also being cut from nearly £30m in 2024-25 to £5m in 2028-29. Aid to Tanzania will be slashed from £60m in 2025-26 to £5m in 2028-29. The Caribbean Development Team will have its funding cut from more than £98m in 2025-26 to £45m in 2026-27.
Nigeria will continue to represent one of the biggest destinations for Commonwealth aid, scheduled to receive £68m in 2028-29, down from £137m this year.

Funding for nature has been particularly hard-hit, experts told the Guardian, as many Commonwealth countries have not only had their aid funding slashed but have also been cut off from applying to the Darwin Initiative funds for nature protection. At least 26 countries from the Commonwealth have been prevented from receiving funds under the longstanding Darwin funding stream, worth about £40m a year.

Adrian Gahan, the UK lead at the Campaign for Nature charity, said: “UK aid to Commonwealth countries has fallen dramatically in recent years, with further cuts on the horizon. Some of the world’s most biodiversity-rich countries, many of which are also grappling with high levels of poverty, are facing severe reductions in support. For example, the UK’s Caribbean Development Team is set to see its funding cut by more than half between this year and next.”

He noted the contrast between the government’s stance at Chogm and the royal visit to the Caribbean. “This week, the king attended the launch of the Commonwealth nature initiative, a major new effort to protect nature across Commonwealth countries,” said Gahan. “Yet the UK government failed to make a financial contribution.”

Jean McLean, Oxfam GB chief influencing officer, said: “The UK government has really dropped the ball when it comes to the aid budget at exactly the moment when conflict, humanitarian crises, hunger and climate breakdown are driving global need to record levels. These cuts will not be felt in Westminster – they will be felt by families facing starvation, children denied healthcare and education, and communities struggling to survive the impacts of conflict and climate disasters.”
The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office has been approached for comment. The Chogm meeting is set to wrap up on Wednesday.

articles.title: Man who drugged and raped wife found many men ‘whose fantasy is an unconscious woman’, court told
articles.summary:
Nine men stand trial in Manchester accused of participating in abuse at couple’s home in Stockport, or encouraging it online

The Stockport man who drugged, raped and sexually assaulted his…
articles.byline: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent

blocks.text: The Stockport man who drugged, raped and sexually assaulted his wife personally found a large number of the “many, many men whose fantasy is an unconscious and unresponsive woman”, a court has heard.
Nine men are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street crown court, accused of either participating in the abuse, which took place at the couple’s home, or encouraging it online.

The husband, who is in his 60s, has pleaded guilty to multiple offences against his wife, committed over a period of more than 20 years. He cannot be named in order to protect the anonymity of his victim.

On the second day of the prosecution case, Louise Oakley KC told the jury the husband had met the first defendant, Robert Stewart, 70, who also lived in Stockport, Greater Manchester, on Craigslist in 2015.

His interaction with Stewart, the jury was told, was “to be his blueprint for future offending”. Stewart had asked if the victim would ever participate in a “threesome”, but the husband “made it clear that there was absolutely no chance of that”, the court heard.

The two men then discussed the use of date rape drugs and opportunities to spike her drink to try to render the woman unconscious. Stewart provided the husband with antidepressants and Tramadol, a strong painkiller, on agreement the husband would invite Stewart to go to their home if she was unconscious, the jury was told.
The contact between the two men was, Oakley said, “no doubt the first big step [the husband] took in realising his own fantasy of having another man come to him and ‘fuck’ his unaware wife.”

The court heard the husband had visited news websites and online forums, where he searched for information on date rape drugs, GHB and sleeping tablets. “[The husband’s] perversity did not wane,” Oakley told the court. “He wanted to share her but recognised that alcohol alone was not going to be enough.

“So desperate, you may think, was he, he would share imagery of [his wife] with complete strangers and then discuss how they would supply him with drugs in order that she be raped. Sharing her, his desire, in their own home.”
The court heard that the husband had also discussed with a second defendant, David Graves, 60, from Ilkeston in Derbyshire, the need to find “something to knock her out completely”.
Graves, described as a “non-contact offender”, had supplied the husband with tablets to drug his wife, and in return the husband agreed to send him imagery of the abuse.

The husband had asked Graves to post the tablets to the house of a close relative of his wife’s who had recently died, the court heard. “The house where [the relative] had been living was empty,” Oakley told the court. “Does it get any worse than that?”

The court heard Graves then became “incredibly impatient” when there was a delay in sending the images. The husband told him “he tried the tablets but they tasted so bitter and his wife thought there was something wrong with the curry,” Oakley said. “Obviously the tablets he had put in the food.”

A third defendant, Philip Wild, 58, from Stockport, had visited the couple’s home in August 2023, the court heard. The husband told him he had to be quiet, so he didn’t wake the victim, and advised him to step out on to the landing if she stirred, and that “he would deal with the situation”.
Wild had touched the woman sexually, and “was fully aware that [she] was not conscious and not able to consent to any sexual activity”, Oakley told the court.

The husband put Wild, a taxi driver, in touch with another man, Graham Brougham, who also lived close to the couple’s Stockport address, the court heard, and they discussed having sex with the woman using WhatsApp.
The name of the WhatsApp group was originally a pseudonym for the woman that her husband had used online, but was later renamed to “Taxi” in an apparent bid to avoid suspicion.
The jury was told the husband also sent pictures of his wife to another “non-contact offender”, Daniel Rayner, 42, from Whitstable in Kent.
Rayner repeatedly asked the husband for images, Oakley said, and “he knows that what he wants, he gets.”

The pair also discussed drugging the victim, and Rayner’s ability to obtain the date rape drug GHB. “[Rayner] knew [the wife] was unaware, and he knew that she was being sexually abused by her husband,” Oakley said.

Five other men are on trial accused of participating in the abuse of the woman. They are Jordan Wallace, 31, from Manchester; Alan Keelan, 42, from Manchester; Jonathan Kirk, 43, from Stockport; Mohammed Sabir, 28, of no fixed abode; and Richard Townsend, 37, from Heywood in Greater Manchester. All of the men on trial deny the charges against them.

Three men – Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport; Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee; and Graham Brougham, 74, from Northwich in Cheshire – have already admitted to abusing the woman, while Karl Lindsay, 56, from Somerset, has pleaded guilty to “non-contact” offences.

“The sad reality of this case is that there are many, many men whose fantasy is an unconscious and unresponsive woman,” Oakley told the court. “[The husband] found a large number of them. We suggest they sit in this dock today.”
While all of the men may not know exactly what drugs the husband had administered, Oakley said, “they expected her to be ‘wasted’ and ‘out of it.’
“The harsh reality is,” Oakley said, “any right-minded human being who walked into that room, that bedroom, with two eyes, two ears, and half a brain would have realised she was not conscious.”
“They knew. It’s what they wanted,” she added. “Anyone who didn’t, would have run a country mile.”
While the defendants may claim the wife had consented, Oakley said, “any defendant that suggests they had any conversation with her, I suggest is lying.”
The trial, which is expected to last for three months, continues.

Cleveland Meredith arrested after allegedly posting a call to execute all judges involved in 2021 US Capitol attack trials

A man pardoned by

blocks.text: A man pardoned by Donald Trump for participating in January 6 attack on the US Capitol and threatening to kill then house speaker Nancy Pelosi is facing new charges for threatening to kill federal judges that presided over his and other cases arising from the violent anti-government clash.
Cleveland Meredith, from North Carolina, was arrested on Monday over a Facebook post in April that allegedly read: “ALL J6 Federal JUDGES will be EXECUTED!”

Then last month, according to the government, Meredith posted “several threatening and concerning messages calling for violence following the midterm elections”, including: “Make damn sure you’re on the right team going into the midterms/… firing squads will commence 11/04/26.”
Another post, noted in the complaint, reads: “The midterms will be an absolute MASSACRE.”
Federal prosecutors in the Georgia, from where the messages was sent, said in the complaint that the message “expressly threatened execution” and “constituted a true threat under the circumstances”.

“Meredith’s history of violent online rhetoric indicates that he knowingly sent the message on April 23, 2026,” the complaint said, alleging that he did so for “the purpose of issuing a threat, with knowledge that his post would be viewed as a threat, or while consciously disregarding a substantial risk that his post would be viewed as a threat”.
In December 2021, Meredith was sentenced to 28 months after pleading guilty to a charge involving a threat he made to shoot Pelosi.
Prosecutors said Meredith had traveled from Colorado to Washington DC on 6 January 2021, but arrived late because of car trouble, missing the confrontation at the US Capitol.

Several days before the riot, Meredith posted his strategy for the insurrection action: “Allow your enemy to be boastful, to think he has won. Present yourself as weak, disorganized. Then eradicate.” That was followed by another Facebook post that read: “We’re gonna surround DC and slowly constrict.”
Then, on 6 January, he wrote: “War time” and “I’m gonna collect a shit ton of Traitors heads.”

The following day he sent a text message to one of his relatives that included a threat directed toward Pelosi. The relative contacted Meredith’s mother, an interior designer whose work has appeared in Southern Living magazine, who then contacted the FBI.

Meredith was then tracked to a hotel near the Capitol. The FBI found a 9mm semi-automatic firearm, an assault-style rifle with a telescopic sight, approximately 2,500 rounds of ammunition and large-capacity magazines inside his trailer.

On his first day back in office in 2025, Trump pardoned Meredith as part of a mass executive clemency order covering nearly 1,600 individuals charged or convicted of seditious conspiracy over their participation in the assault.
after newsletter promotion
Prosecutors said Meredith’s April Facebook post was part of a campaign.
“The Defendant has been threatening and harassing individuals and institutions online for at least the last sixteen months,” they said in a motion to hold Meredith in detention.

He had been referred to the FBI in July 2025 for making a threat to an unnamed individual, prosecutors said, and was interviewed by the bureau. Meredith “acknowledged making them but denied they were threatening in nature”, according to the government.
Meredith is one of a number of Trump’s J6 defendants who received pardons and have, or allegedly have, reoffended.
Prior to the January 6 riot, Meredith had run Car Nutz, an Atlanta-area car-wash business. The business attracted controversy in 2018 when it sponsored a billboard linking itself to QAnon.
Asked why he had linked his car-wash business to the conspiracy theory umbrella, Meredith told the Atlanta Journal-Constitution: “We all support freedom and independent thought.”

articles.title: Protect Poundland from predatory capitalism, MPs tell government
articles.summary:
Budget retailer and 12,000 jobs at risk after US owner fails to accept buyout offers

MPs have called on the government to protect

blocks.text: MPs have called on the government to protect Poundland and other high street stores from “predatory capitalism” and asset-stripping.

The fate of the retail chain and its 12,000 staff remains uncertain after it filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators at the high court last Thursday. The US restructuring specialist Gordon Brothers, which controls Poundland, has lined up the advisory company AlixPartners to run the process.

In an urgent question in the House of Commons on Tuesday, Gareth Snell, Labour MP for Stoke-on-Trent Central, asked the government what could be done to “send a message to Gordon Brothers that the predatory capitalism that they are putting into this company will not be tolerated, because we in this country will always stand with people before profit”.

Another Labour MP, Antonia Bance, asked what measures the government would use to “hold Gordon Brothers to account”, and if it would “establish an urgent review of whether our corporate governance and insolvency frameworks give sufficient protection against asset stripping and short term financial engineering, at the cost of jobs and our high streets?”

The Green party MP Hannah Spencer said the “scandal” of Poundland “exposes a very serious problem, that our economy is vulnerable to private equity vultures who swoop in and prey on our high street brands by loading them with debt and then trying to ditch them for a profit”.

Kate Dearden, minister for the future of work, told parliament that government officials had held talks with Gordon Brothers on Monday night and she would meet Poundland’s management team along with Usdaw, the shop workers’ union, on Wednesday.
She said Jonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, would meet Gordon Brothers again later this week as political pressure mounts on the company to accept a solvent bid for Poundland.
Dearden said the government could not involve itself in the “commercial negotiations” with potential buyers or comment on individual bids.

However, she said the government was “taking a responsible approach not to sit by and do nothing” and was putting pressure on Gordon Brothers to accept it had “responsibilities as well as rights” over Poundland and its employees.
Gordon Brothers is understood to remain in talks with at least two potential buyers for the whole company, including a fully funded offer from Northern Ireland’s Martin Property Group.
Another offer from Innovest, an investment group understood to be advised by former Reform election candidate Charles Bunker, is believed to have partial funding in place.
The chance of Poundland avoiding mass store closures and job losses is shrinking by the day because suppliers have held back on deliveries, hurting its ability to trade.
Gordon Brothers is believed to be unwilling to accept Martin Property’s offer of about £15m, only half of which would be paid immediately, because it falls short of repaying a £30m shareholder loan.
The prime minister’s spokesperson said: “We continue to stay close to what’s an extremely worrying situation for Poundland staff, their families and communities.
after newsletter promotion

“Gordon Brothers need to explain why they haven’t accepted any offer to keep the company going. That’s the case. It appears they’re not acting in the best interests of their loyal UK staff and stores.”

In a letter to the government, reported by Sky News, Gordon Brothers executive Mark Newton-Jones defended its approach, saying it had “supported Poundland with £85m of additional financing” since acquiring it for £1 last year and the chain had returned to underlying profit.

However, the letter added: “Like other high street retailers, the company faces multiple economic challenges, including rising inflation, increasing staffing costs and shrinkage from severe levels of shoplifting, which means it is still not cash-generative at a sustainable level despite the turnaround efforts.”
Dozens of MPs from around the UK have called on the government to reassure their constituents that action would be taken to stop Poundland’s collapse.
Bradley Thomas, the Conservative party business spokesperson, blamed the government for Poundland’s demise. He said: “The current economic landscape is hostile to British business.”
Earlier on Tuesday, the founder of Poundland, Steve Smith, told the Guardian that staff at the chain could be out of work for years if it collapsed.
Gordon Brothers was approached for comment.

articles.title: Vivienne Jolie drops dad Brad Pitt's last name, following 3 other siblings
articles.summary: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt's daughter, Vivienne, has officially dropped her father's last name, making her the fourth child of the former celebrity couple to do so.

image.caption: Vivienne Jolie, the daughter of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, seen here in 2024 with her mother, has officially dropped 'Pitt' from her last name. (Eduardo Munoz/Reuters)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt's daughter, Vivienne, has officially dropped her father's last name, making her the fourth child of the former celebrity couple to do so.
Vivienne Jolie is the 4th child of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt to change their last name
The 18-year-old will now be known as Vivienne Marcheline Jolie, instead of Vivienne Marcheline Jolie-Pitt, according to documents obtained by CBC News.

She initially filed a petition with the Los Angeles County Superior Court to legally drop her father's last name back in July, shortly after her 18th birthday, with the reason for the change listed as "personal."

Four of the six now-adult children shared by Jolie and Pitt have changed their names, effectively legally distancing themselves from their father amid ongoing tensions in the wake of the couple's 2016 split and ensuing legal battle, which included allegations from Jolie that Pitt had been abusive toward her and the children in a 2016 incident.
Pitt was investigated for child abuse at the time and cleared of all wrongdoing.

Vivienne has been using only her mother's last name for at least two years — she was credited as Vivienne Jolie for her work as a volunteer production assistant on the Broadway show The Outsiders, which her mother co-produced.

items: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt’s daughter Vivienne files to drop Pitt's last name
Zahara Jolie files to legally drop Brad Pitt's name

blocks.text: Judge Virginia Keeny granted Vivienne's petition during a hearing on Monday at the Los Angeles Superior Court's Stanley Mosk Courthouse.
Angelina Jolie poses with her children, from left, Maddox, Vivienne, Zahara, Shiloh and Knox at the premiere for the film Eternals in Los Angeles on Oct. 18, 2021. (Mario Anzuoni/Reuters)
Vivienne, along with her twin brother, Knox, is the youngest of Pitt and Jolie's children. The others are Maddox, 24; Pax, 22; Zahara, 21; and Shiloh, 20.
Shiloh was the first child to drop the Pitt name in 2024. Zahara and Maddox both filed earlier this year, and had the petitions granted in September.

Jolie and Pitt, once one of the most high-profile couples in Hollywood, married in 2014 after a decade together. Jolie filed for divorce in 2016 and a judge declared them legally single in 2019, but their contentious split wasn't completely settled until 2024.

items: Katie Holmes and Tom Cruise's daughter, Suri, drops Cruise's last name

blocks.text: The divorce filing came after an alleged incident on a plane in 2016, the details of which were outlined in court documents filed in 2022. Jolie alleged in the filings that Pitt had grabbed Jolie, pushed her, and choked one of their children and struck another when they tried to intervene. A representative for Pitt denied the allegations, and the FBI stated it had conducted a review and was not pursuing further investigation.
Brad Pitt attends the European premiere for F1: The Movie in London on June 23, 2025. (Maja Smiejkowska/Reuters)
While Jolie has appeared frequently with the children on red carpets, Pitt has not been seen in public with any of his children for years.

The 62-year-old actor has not publicly addressed the name changes of his children. In an August interview with Esquire, he alluded to it, saying he had briefly experienced suicidal ideation over "family stuff," and "didn't see a way out."

The six children have largely kept out of the spotlight and avoided speaking about their family or relationships with either parent. Earlier this year, Zahara praised mother Jolie, 51, during a mother-daughter brunch for the Pearls of Purpose Foundation in Atlanta, saying their relationship was a "kindred" one.
Angelina Jolie and Zahara Marley Jolie attend the 82nd Golden Globe Awards in Beverly Hills on Jan. 5, 2025. (Daniel Cole/Reuters)
"She's the most selfless, loving and understanding woman, who I get to call my mom," she said.

According to People, she ended the speech by turning and directly addressing Jolie, who was in attendance: "I think back to a quote I saw years ago that said, 'I am a strong woman because a strong woman raised me.' Thank you, Mom."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Alexandra Mae Jones is a senior writer for CBC News based in Toronto. She has written on a variety of topics, from health to pop culture to breaking news, and previously reported for CTV News and the Toronto Star. She joined CBC in 2024. You can reach her at alexandra.mae.jones@cbc.ca

articles.title: Trump says US will end military aid to Israel by the end of this year
articles.summary:
US president makes surprise election day announcement, saying country does not ‘need’ $4bn annual payment

Donald Trump has said that the US will end military aid to Israel at the end of this…

blocks.text: Donald Trump has said that the US will end military aid to Israel at the end of this year in a surprise election day announcement that appeared to be targeted at voters sceptical of US support for Israel and the war in Gaza.
In a phone interview with Fox News as voting began on Tuesday morning, Trump said the US would cut nearly $4bn (£2.96bn) in military aid to Israel because “they don’t need it.”
“We were giving them $4bn … But it gets cut off at the end of the year,” he said.

Trump also indicated that he had decided to end the aid – which he claimed would be replaced by arms sales to Israel instead – because it had become a popular criticism of US foreign policy led by outspoken candidates including the Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.
“Why should we suffer the slings from lunatics like El-Sayed when they don’t need it?” Trump said. “It’s a bad talking point.”

blocks.caption: Abdul El-Sayed, pictured campaigning on Monday, would become the US’s first Muslim senator if elected. Photograph: Zach D Roberts/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

blocks.text: During the interview, Trump claimed that the abrupt ending of aid was proposed by Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. “We give them $4bn of things and money, and they don’t need it,” he said. “And I was approached by Bibi Netanyahu, and we’ve been talking about it for a couple of years because it’s a lot of money.”
Netanyahu had previously suggested tapering off US military aid to Israel over the next decade, but Trump’s announcement on Tuesday would significantly accelerate that timeline.

Israel received most of the approximately $3.8bn in 2025 as Foreign Military Financing grants that allow the country to buy US military hardware including F-35 fighter jets. Another $500m was given for joint missile defence programmes.

Trump’s announcement on Tuesday appeared timed to affect the outcome of the midterm elections, where US foreign policy and support for Israel have played an unusually important role in key races, including the Michigan senatorial race where El-Sayed is running against Republican Mike Rogers. He would become the country’s first Muslim senator if he is elected.
after newsletter promotion

A Quinnipiac University poll released in September showed that 48% of Americans believed that the US was too supportive of Israel, and other recent polls have shown a historic shift away from US support for Israel and Netanyahu’s government.

Anger over the humanitarian crisis in Gaza has helped usher in a wave of progressive Democratic candidates including El-Sayed, and Trump’s vice-president JD Vance has openly accused Israel of trying to sabotage US negotiations with Iran. In a June interview with the New York Times, Vance said of Israel’s foreign policy: “You can’t just kill your way out of solving every single national security problem that you have.”

During his Fox News interview, Trump spoke warmly about Netanyahu and also boasted about his own popularity in Israel. “If people ever got tired of me in the US, I’ll move to Israel and become prime minister,” he said.

articles.summary: At least 250 pet owners have filed complaints against Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium before the Bacoor City Police Station in connection with alleged irregularities in its handling of deceased…

blocks.text: Published November 4, 2026 1:04am

At least 250 pet owners have filed complaints against Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium before the Bacoor City Police Station in connection with alleged irregularities in its handling of deceased pets, authorities said.

Bacoor City Police Station chief PLTCOL Alexie Desamito reported that the number of complainants who formally approached the police has reached 250, according to a social media post by Bacoor Mayor Strike Revilla.

In the initial phase of the investigation, Revilla said complainants turned over 20 containers of ashes from their pets to authorities. These are now undergoing forensic examination by the Philippine National Police Forensic Group.
Separately, authorities recovered 29 dog carcasses during an operation in San Jose del Monte, Bulacan.
Nine of the carcasses have so far been positively identified by their respective pet owners, while verification and identification of the remaining carcasses are ongoing.

The Bacoor City government thanked the local police and National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Alvarez Matibag for assisting in the investigation and efforts to hold those responsible accountable.
Authorities have yet to disclose further details as the investigation continues. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Officials investigate fire at Mississippi police department tied to fatal shooting of Black toddler
articles.summary:
Person arrested after fire at police department where officer who shot and killed one-year-old Kohen Wiley had worked

In the early hours of 31 October, a fire broke out at the Senatobia…

blocks.text: In the early hours of 31 October, a fire broke out at the Senatobia police department in Mississippi, which has been embroiled in controversy recently after one of its officers shot and killed Kohen Wiley, a one-year-old. Though the cause of the fire has not been reported, it is being investigated as arson by agents with the US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.

In June, then Senatobia police sergeant Hunter Foster shot Kohen as he sat in his mother’s arms in a Walmart parking lot. Foster, who is white, was responding to a report of an alleged shoplifting; Kohen, his mother and the driver of the vehicle, are Black.
An arrest tied to the fire was made on Monday, but no details about the person of interest have been released. The Senatobia police department did not respond to a request for comment.
Shortly after Kohen was killed in June, activists and community members led protests, including one outside the Senatobia police department, in hopes of receiving answers about the shooting.

The Mississippi bureau of investigation, which investigated the shooting, alleged that the driver of the vehicle in which Kohen sat “drove in the direction of the officers, almost striking one”. However, civil rights attorney Ben Crump, who is representing the Wiley family, released an independent autopsy that indicated Kohen was shot from the side of the car, not the front.
In mid-October, Lynn Fitch, Mississippi’s attorney general, announced in a statement that the shooting was “justified”. Foster resigned from the police force shortly after Fitch’s statement.

“After what I’ve seen today, I’m having a difficult time understanding the word ‘justified’,” LaSandra Williams, Kohen’s paternal grandmother, said during a press conference Crump held about video footage of the shooting. “I don’t understand how it’s OK for someone to take a sweet, innocent soul – Lord knows I miss him so much.”

The shooting was just the most recent in a series of incidents involving Senatobia’s police force. The month prior to Fitch’s statement, Senatobia, which is about 40% Black, fired its police chief, who allegedly used racial slurs.

A year before Kohen was killed, at the same Walmart, an officer forced a Black woman from her car and pointed a stun gun at her in front of her children after she parked in a handicap space to wait for her grandmother, who was shopping in the store. The woman was driving a vehicle with a handicap parking tag.
And in 2023, an officer arrested and placed in a cell a 10-year-old Black boy who had urinated in public. The child was later sentenced to three months’ probation.

Kohen would have turned two last weekend. The Senatobia Committee for Accountability and Transparency, an activist group, organized a giveaway at the city’s community center to celebrate what would have been the toddler’s birthday. Families who attended received diapers, wipes, food and other items.
The ongoing investigation into the fire is being handled by the US attorney general’s office of the northern district of Mississippi.

articles.title: Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital
articles.summary: At least 38 people are killed in 24 hours and Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky warns dozens more could be trapped under rubble.

blocks.text: Russian strikes on Ukraine – including on an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital – have killed at least 38 civilians and injured scores of others across Ukraine over the last 24 hours.

At least 33 people are known to have died in a glide bomb attack in the southern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday night, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said the number of victims was set to rise as more than 50 people could be trapped under the rubble.
He called the strike in Komyshuvakha village "one of the largest mass killings committed by Russia during this war".
Ukraine had proposed to extend and expand last week's ceasefire in the Kherson region which allowed people from the frontline Russian-occupied town of Oleshky to evacuate, Zelensky added.
The attack on a school building being used as an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha was Moscow's response, he said.
Elsewhere, a hospice was attacked in the central city of Dnipro and a hospital was hit in the north-eastern city of Kharkiv, where Zelensky said 73 people were wounded, most of them elderly patients.

Nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit Komyshuvakha as residents were gathering to receive humanitarian aid at a distribution centre, authorities said. Local media reported that when the attack began, people took refuge underground but the roof collapsed, trapping many underneath.
"The scale of the tragedy is difficult to comprehend," regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.
Russia's defense ministry said the attack had targeted Ukrainian military units and killed 25 servicemen.

However, there was no credible evidence that the site was being used by the Ukrainian military and there were no major military or industrial facilities in the settlement of Komyshuvakha, reports BBC News Russian defence correspondent Ilya Abishev.
The village is to the south-east of the city of Zaporizhzhia, which has come under constant Russian bombardment.
According to Abishev, Komyshuvakha is of high military importance as part of Ukraine's defensive and transport network on the approaches to the regional capital.

But the UN's human rights monitoring mission said the distribution of humanitarian aid at the local school had been highly publicised and the attack "seems to have violated the most fundamental principles of international humanitarian law", external.

Further north, in Dnipro, nearly 50 terminally ill patients were being transferred to other facilities after their hospice was destroyed by a Russian missile on Monday night. The oldest of the patients was 90 years old.
Mayor Boris Filatov posted photos on Telegram showing elderly people lying in their beds in a hospice room with blown-out windows and rubble and broken glass strewn on the floors.
"I realise that I am violating ethics," wrote Filatov. "I want as many people as possible to see these photos. Especially politicians and diplomats. Especially abroad.
"These are elderly, terminally ill people. This is a Russian missile."
Elsewhere in Dnipro, a separate strike killed two people and left 18 others wounded. Another five people were killed in aerial bomb and drone strikes on Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region.
Russia has also struck energy infrastructure in nine regions, affecting water and heating.

The water supply in Kyiv was entirely cut off "due to enemy attacks and damage to the capital's energy infrastructure", the main water supplier Kyivvodokanal said. The entire metro network was suspended on Tuesday and Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the situation surrounding the city's power supply was becoming "very difficult".
As Ukraine was counting its dead, the Kremlin announced it would take part in three-way peace talks with Ukraine brokered by the US in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November.
It will be the first trilateral meeting since February. Since then, Russia and the US have begun engaging more directly, with US President Donald Trump announcing a deal to import Russian diesel.

Speaking to reporters in Berlin on Tuesday, Zelensky said that it was important for Russia to engage seriously in negotiations on a ceasefire and a peaceful settlement, but that he had so far had not seen "any indication" of that being the case.

Several rounds of ceasefire talks late last year yielded no results, and in public declarations Russian officials have generally refused to budge from Moscow's maximalist demand of effective Ukrainian surrender.

US First Lady Melania Trump Melania Trump, who was credited with brokering a truce last week in the besieged town of Oleshky, is set to host representatives of Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday. However, no details were given in the White House statement of who was due to attend the meeting., external
The UN said last month that civilian casualties in Ukraine had reached a "record level", as Russian armed forces resumed systematic attacks on energy infrastructure.

Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Its advances on the front line have since stalled, and attacks on Ukraine have intensified, with Moscow employing large numbers of missiles and drones to strike Ukrainian cities.
At the same time, Ukraine is faces a critical air defense shortage due to stalled Western deliveries of weapons and a lack of American Patriot interceptor missiles.

In Berlin, Zelensky acknowledged that although the front line was stable "the situation in the air was not as positive, particularly when it comes to our air defence capabilities and the protection of our civilian population".

articles.title: PWHL star Sarah Fillier expected to play for Canada at world championship
articles.summary: Canadian forward Sarah Fillier is expected to play at the world championship that begins on Friday in Denmark. The New York Sirens star is listed as day to day with an upper body injury she sustained…

image.caption: Canadian forward Sarah Fillier (10) is expected to play in the world championship that begins on Friday in Denmark. The New York Sirens star sustained an injury early in a 4-0 loss to the U.S. in a pre-tournament game last Friday. (Nathan Denette/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: PWHL·New

Canadian forward Sarah Fillier is expected to play at the world championship that begins on Friday in Denmark. The New York Sirens star is listed as day to day with an upper body injury she sustained early in a 4-0 pre-tournament loss to the United States last Friday.
Forward was injured early in a 4-0 pre-tournament loss to the U.S. on Friday
Canadian star Sarah Fillier is expected to play at the world championship as Canada looks to reclaim gold from the United States.
Fillier left Friday's pre-tournament game against the U.S. after going into the boards awkwardly. The Canadians went on to lose that game, 4-0.
The New York Sirens forward looked to be clutching her right shoulder or arm as she exited the game. The team has described the ailment as an upper-body injury.
Canadian GM Danièle Sauvageau said Fillier is considered day to day, so it's not yet clear when she may suit up for Canada. The team's first game is against Sweden on Friday at 9 a.m. ET in Denmark.
"Things are looking good, so it's a question of day by day," Sauvageau told CBC Sports on Tuesday. "It's on a good track, a positive track."

Fillier scored the game-winning goal and added an assist in Canada's 5-3 pre-tournament win over the U.S. last Wednesday, which ended an eight-game American winning streak that dated back to February 2025.

items: U.S. blanks Canada in warm-up ahead of women's world hockey championship
Canada earns victory over U.S. in exhibition game ahead of women's hockey worlds

blocks.text: That she hasn't been ruled out for the tournament is a big win for the Canadians, who rely on Fillier to drive offence on the top line and first-unit power play. Sauvageau described her as a "young veteran" on an increasingly younger Team Canada.
At the Olympics, Fillier finished second in team points (six in seven games), behind Daryl Watts.
Rebuilding for 2030

Canada also has 20-year-old Colgate University forward Alexia Aubin practising with the team in Denmark, but that is unrelated to Fillier's injury. The decision to bring Aubin as an alternate was made before Fillier was hurt.
Canadian women's hockey team loses exhibition to U.S. ahead of world championships
An alternate can replace an injured player at any point during the tournament, assuming the injured player can't return for the rest of the tournament.
But Aubin was also brought to get experience with the team, as the Canadians rebuild ahead of the 2030 Olympics in the French Alps.
"We want to expose as many players as possible in order to be the most prepared," Sauvageau said.

The Canadians looked disconnected in Friday's game, struggling to break the puck out cleanly and generate high-danger chances. The Americans outshot them, 32-13, and Canada's penalty kill yielded two goals on five opportunities.
But the Canadians are keeping the bigger picture in mind, with so many new, young players getting their first crack at international play on the senior team.

"It is an exhibition game," Sauvageau said about Friday's loss. "It is a game that, again, we need to expose, we need to try different things. Of course, Team USA played very, very well and this is what we expected. But at the end of the day, we need to play games in order to get better and to create cohesion, and give the players the experience that we're going to continue to build on."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Karissa Donkin is a reporter with CBC Sports who covers the PWHL, women's hockey and lots more. You can reach her at karissa.donkin@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Primark brings forward home deliveries plan by two years after profits slide
articles.summary:
Retailer acquires robot-assisted warehouse and intends to have UK service up and running before end of 2027

Primark is to begin making home deliveries by the end of next year as it aims to…

blocks.text: Primark is to begin making home deliveries by the end of next year as it aims to win new shoppers after a slide in profits.
George Weston, the boss of the cut-price fashion chain’s owner Associated British Foods (ABF), said it had brought forward the launch of Primark’s home delivery plans by about two years.
The company was able to speed up the process by snapping up a robot-assisted warehouse in Sheffield from Debenhams, the owner of Boohoo, PrettyLittle Thing and Karen Millen.

Primark will take over the warehouse by the middle of next year and is working on preparing its suppliers to provide stock suitable for sending out to individual shoppers as well as the usual bulk orders for stores.
Primark already offers a click and collect service in the UK which it has gradually rolled out since 2022. The service is not available to its stores in mainland Europe.

The chain, which has 511 stores across 21 countries, will launch home deliveries in the UK by December next year. It intends to offer the service in mainland Europe after that, but has not set out a timeframe.

Primark has previously said it could not make money by selling fashion for home delivery, but Weston said the economics had changed with delivery and returns charges that could cover most of the logistical costs now common across the industry.

He added that the group’s research had shown it could attract new customers, rather than just substituting a sale in store for a less profitable one online. “We now know there’s a group of shoppers who don’t reject Primark but just don’t use us very often as they are too far away from a store or prefer to shop online,” he said.

The move comes as Primark faces tough competition from the rise of cut-price online specialists such as Shein as well as the supermarkets’ clothing ranges and the likes of H&M and Zara, all of which sell online and in stores.
Weston insisted that Shein was not grabbing more than a “little bit” of market share from Primark, and that there was more competition from those who could mix online and stores.
after newsletter promotion

Sales at Primark rose 4% to £9.8bn in the year to 12 September led by new store openings. Sales at established UK stores rose just 0.5% and sales at established stores in mainland Europe slumped 4.7% and in the US were down 2.6% as shoppers reined in spending on clothing amid higher energy and fuel bills.

Primark said performance in the UK had been helped by improved ranges, action to cut prices and more marketing, tactics that are now being rolled out across Europe. However, that action saw profits drop 10% to £1bn.
ABF intends to spin off Primark in December 2027, separating it from its sugar and food business that includes brands such as Twinings teas, Blue Dragon flavourings and Jordans cereals.

The 26-year-old Bayern Munich defender is one of 23 players on the roster unveiled by head coach Jesse Marsch on Tuesday.

Davies played limited minutes for the national team at this summer's World Cup as he recovered from a hamstring injury, and he missed Canada's three friendlies in late September and early October for his honeymoon.

Canada, currently ranked 27th in the world, will visit No. 95 Guatemala to open the two-legged series on Nov. 13 before hosting the second leg at Toronto's BMO Field on Nov. 16.

blocks.text: They will snap and they will crackle, but they may no longer pop, as Kellogg’s has removed rice from its Rice Krispies and Coco Pops cereals due to “changing weather conditions”.

Rice Krispies has been reformulated to use rice flour instead of rice, while Coco Pops now contain a blend of rice flour and corn flour instead of rice in order to maintain consistent quality. Kelloggs’ said the shift reflected how the climate crisis had affected the quality and availability of some rice and grains used in its most popular cereals.

A spokesperson for Kellogg’s said: “We have updated the Rice Krispies and Coco Pops recipes, which are now made using corn flour and rice flour. We appreciate that even small changes to a much-loved product can feel noticeable and that’s why we have approached this with a lot of care and consideration.
“The updated recipes have been carefully assessed for taste, appearance and texture, and we are continuing to listen closely to consumer feedback.”

Kellogg’s said both cereals remained “non-HFSS” – or not high in fat, salt or sugar – contained no artificial colours, flavours or sweeteners and maintained the same levels of fibre, Vitamin D and iron.
The new recipes will also contain wheat gluten, meaning they are no longer suitable for shoppers with a wheat allergy or coeliac disease.

Previously, Rice Krispies and Coco Pops were labelled “may contain gluten” because they were made in a factory where other cereals containing gluten were also handled. As wheat gluten is now an ingredient, wheat will be declared as an allergen on pack and highlighted in bold in the ingredients list. Both cereals now carry prominent labelling on their packs alerting consumers to the change.
after newsletter promotion
The reformulation comes as sales of Rice Krispies are in decline, with both value and volume down, according to the Grocer magazine’s top products survey 2026, which comes out next month.

articles.title: 7 Montreal police officers have been fired after misconduct allegations. What comes next?
articles.summary: The firings are a result of an internal disciplinary investigation and were carried out on an administrative level — but the criminal investigations, which are separate, are ongoing, said Montreal…

image.caption: In an interview on CBC’s Daybreak Tuesday morning, Dagher called the move to simultaneously fire the seven officers “historic,” saying it had never been done in Montreal. (CBC)

blocks.text: Montreal

The firings are a result of an internal disciplinary investigation and were carried out on an administrative level — but the criminal investigations, which are separate, are ongoing, said Montreal police Chief Fady Dagher.
2 officers dismissed from Station 21, 5 from Station 39

In an interview on CBC's Daybreak Tuesday morning, Montreal police Chief Fady Dagher called the move to simultaneously fire seven Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) officers "historic," saying it had never been done in the city before.

On Monday, Dagher had announced the administrative dismissal of five officers from Station 39, as well as two officers from Station 21, in connection with allegations of discriminatory and racist behaviour, as well as derogatory acts.
On Tuesday, he said accountability was important not just to the public, but also to the rest of the force.
"I want to make sure that some part of the culture of the police stays, because there was magnificent, good work being done by police officers," he said.

items: 7 Montreal police officers dismissed over racist, discriminatory conduct

blocks.text: Montreal police Chief Fady Dagher says efforts have been made to weed out the 1% of police officers who deliberately tarnish the uniform. (CBC)

He said the dismissed police officers will not receive compensation in connection with their dismissals, and they will be required to disclose that they had been the subject of an investigation which resulted in their termination if they sought employment with another police force.
Further action regarding the seven officers could come as the result of other investigations, including the possibility of criminal charges.
Demonstrators kneel outside Station 39 in Montréal-Nord during a protest over allegations of racist conduct involving SPVM officers under investigation. (Paula Dayan-Perez/CBC)

The SPVM has forwarded a file to the Directeur des poursuites criminelles et pénales (DPCP) for it to review charges related to allegations of discriminatory and racist acts against police officers at Station 39.
"We've been digging and digging and digging to find out those kinds of stories, allegations," Dagher said. "We didn't find any more after six, seven months."

Last week, however, it was revealed that the DPCP is investigating another Station 39 officer who, according to Radio-Canada sources, allegedly deleted evidence from a victim's phone in a case of domestic violence in 2025.
When an officer flagged the deletion to her superiors the issue was initially ignored, according to Radio-Canada.

Dagher said that a new action plan is underway to rebuild trust, and that community consultations will be undertaken, especially with people served by Station 39, the station where the majority of the fired officers had worked.
Montreal police chief reveals more about what led to 7 SPVM officers getting fired
The plan, which is expected by the end of December, will outline revisions to the force's recruitment, training and promotion processes.
Dagher said that despite a series of allegations, the SPVM's most recent annual review was the best in the city's last 15 years.

But according to Alain Babineau, former Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer and director of a racial profiling and public safety at the Red Coalition, action on the seven fired officers could have come sooner.
Montrealers protests police misconduct on Oct. 24. (Kwabena Oduro/CBC)
"There's been plans over the last 20 years. Every five years the SPVM has come up with a plan to curb racism, discrimination," he said. "People are tired of plans."
He said that rather than praising police officers for doing work they're expected to do, Dagher should spend time reassuring the communities his officers serve.

"This is not seven bad apples," Babineau said. "Until you actually dismantle the system that has produced those folks, that had allowed those folks to perpetrate these criminal acts, then you can't be totally satisfied."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Hayley Carolan is a journalist based in Montreal.

articles.title: Irish Olympian Ciara Mageean was a 'talented and inspirational human being'
articles.summary: The former European champion and two-time Olympic runner had been diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer.

blocks.text: Olympian Ciara Mageean was a 'talented and inspirational human being'

blocks.caption: Image caption, Ciara Mageean's funeral took place in Portaferry, County Down

blocks.text: Image source, Press Association
Ciara Mageean's funeral took place in Portaferry, County Down
ByCormac Campbell
BBC News NI south east reporter
Olympian Ciara Mageean has been described as a "truly remarkable, immensely talented and inspirational human being" in a tribute read out at her funeral.
Hundreds of people have paid their respects to the runner at her funeral on Tuesday.
The former European champion and two-time Olympic runner died on Sunday after she was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer.

Among those in attendance at the funeral in Portaferry, County Down, were Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill, as well as fellow Olympian Rhys McClenaghan and 1972 gold medallist Lady Mary Peters.
Mageean's funeral cortege was given a guard of honour by Portaferry GAC and her former school, Assumption Grammar in Ballynahinch.

blocks.caption: A close up of the order of service for Ciara Mageean. Hands are holding the missalette up. Photos of Mageean are on the front and back.

blocks.text: Image source, Pacemaker
Her death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to her long-term partner Thomas Moran.
Mourners began arriving at around midday for the 2:00 GMT requiem Mass at St Patrick's Church.
Family, friends and those wishing to pay their respects followed the funeral cortege the short distance along the Ballyphilip Road from Mageean's family home to the church.

Others in attendance included representatives for Irish President Catherine Connolly and the Irish Government, Social Democratic and Labour Party leader Claire Hanna, GAA President Jarlath Burns and former boxer Paddy Barnes.

blocks.caption: Image caption, European champion Ciara Mageean died surrounded by her loved ones at the weekend

blocks.text: Image source, PA
European champion Ciara Mageean died surrounded by her loved ones at the weekend
The Mass booklet included an image of Mageean's greatest achievement on the track, the moment she crossed the line at the 2024 European Championships.
In his homily, Fr Martin Kelly, who knew Mageean from her childhood, spoke of her accomplishments, her love for her husband and the joy and pride she had brought to her hometown.
The athlete represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics and won gold in the 1500m at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in 2024.
She also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning silver in Birmingham in 2022.
What are bowel cancer symptoms?
Noticing blood in your poo - which may appear black or dark red in the toilet bowl - can be a sign of bowel cancer.
If there is no other obvious cause for the bleeding, such as piles, the NHS recommends that you ask for an appointment with your GP, external.
The NHS also advises a check-up if you notice changes in your regular toilet habits, such as having to poo more often, or a pattern of diarrhoea or constipation.
Abdominal pain or lumps, stomach bloating and unexplained weight loss are also among symptoms which should lead to a bowel cancer test.
Bowel cancer can also cause anaemia, the features of which include extreme tiredness and shortness of breath.
The earlier bowel cancer is detected, the easier it is to treat.

articles.title: Binance says fake job interviews used as part of $6.3bn crypto hack
articles.summary: An engineer was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform and invited to bogus job interviews with fake company representatives, Binance says.

blocks.text: Hackers who stole a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from Binance used fake job interviews and a compromised internal AI tool, the firm has revealed.
Initial findings published by the company, which operates the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said hackers gained access to its systems through "sophisticated, multi-stage campaign".

It said they used a range of techniques such as malicious software downloads to compromise the computers of Binance engineers and gain control over tools to drain its wallet of billions of dollars worth of crypto.
Binance called it a "serious and highly sophisticated security incident" and apologised, saying "this should not have happened".
In a post on X, external, Binance said hackers targeted its engineers using social engineering techniques.
These see hackers use approaches such as phishing to trick people into parting with sensitive or personal details, that can then be used to try and access their accounts.
Binance said as part of the hack, one of its engineers was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform and invited to bogus job interviews with fake company representatives.
It said the perpetrators used "more advanced and deceptive" methods to build trust with him, such as sharing social media accounts that contained personal images.
The engineer in question was instructed to download malware masquerading as an "assignment" during a second interview, that deployed malicious code with "obfuscation techniques" evading detection.

Binance said hackers then leveraged the engineer's compromised computer and a compromised internal AI tool in October to gain control over two other engineers' laptops, and execute the next steps of the attack.
The incident led Binance to suspend withdrawals for customers globally, meaning users could not get their cryptocurrency out of the platform until the service was restored on Sunday.
Customers withdrew billions of dollars worth of assets after it reopened.
"We apologise for the concern, disruption and uncertainty it caused our users, partners and the wider industry," it said.
The company added it had taken a range of steps following the incident, including working with law enforcement to trace and freeze affected assets.
It said it had also set aside more than 100% of the funds needed to cover the loss, noting 98% of the token assets impacted had been "replenished" as of Saturday.
The record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) attack is thought to be the largest crypto hack to date.
US crime agencies, including the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Secret Service, have been assisting Binance in tracing the crypto taken from the platform's own wallets.
The agencies, along with a range of cyber analysts, said that the hack - like similar breaches before it - bore the signs of having been orchestrated by North Korea.
Pyongyang hit back at the claims on Tuesday, denying it was behind the hack.

Kim Yo Jong, a top Democratic People's Republic of Korea official and the sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on the accusations were another "sinister attempt" by the US to damage North Korea's public image.
The country has consistently denied being behind a number of major cyber attacks it has been blamed for in recent years.
The TraderTraitor unit, which is also known as the Lazarus Group, was blamed for a then-record $1.5bn hack of crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.
Binance had previously not responded to the BBC's queries about North Korea's alleged involvement in the hack.

But on Tuesday, the company wrote in its post on X, external: "The latest information released by the Federal Bureau of Investigation indicates that the Democratic People's Republic of Korea is responsible for this incident."

As part of its security efforts following the attack, Binance said it would also increase investment in AI tools that can detect security threats, as well as engage third-party cyber experts to carry out a full-scale review of the incident.
It also said that it would seek to stablish a security research fund and work with leading AI and security firms on targeted initiatives.

articles.title: QC aligns heat-related class suspension rules with DepEd, Marcos EO
articles.summary: The Quezon City government is aligning its heat-related class suspension guidelines with a Department of Education (DepEd) directive and an executive order signed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.,…

blocks.text: Published November 4, 2026 12:11am

The Quezon City government is aligning its heat-related class suspension guidelines with a Department of Education (DepEd) directive and an executive order signed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., allowing schools to independently suspend in-person classes during bad weather and under hazardous conditions.
The city government said it was revoking Memorandum Circular No. 3, Series of 2025, on heat-related class suspensions to comply with DepEd Memorandum No. 064, Series of 2026.

Under the DepEd directive, public school heads may adjust class schedules, suspend face-to-face classes or shift to alternative learning modes based on conditions in their respective schools, in coordination with the Schools Division Office.
Private schools are also encouraged to adopt the guidelines, as applicable.

"Parents, guardians, and learners are advised to monitor their schools’ official communication channels for announcements on class schedules and learning arrangements," the QC government said in a statement.
"The City Government will also comply with Executive Order No. 130 and awaits its implementing guidelines to ensure proper implementation," it added.

Executive Order No. 130 allows schools to declare localized suspensions of in-person classes when national or local governments have not issued a suspension order, provided site-specific conditions indicate an actual or imminent threat to the safety, health, or welfare of learners and school personnel.

Aside from granular suspension, schools may automatically suspend on-site classes and work upon issuance of any warning, advisory, alert level, or forecast by PAGASA, PHIVOLCS, or DENR-Environmental Management Bureau.
Moreover, local officials may declare suspensions based on the specific, verified disaster or risk levels within their respective city, municipality, or province.
However, the EO provides that schools should implement learning continuity measures despite the suspension of in-person classes or activities.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: 295 DPWH projects to be removed
articles.summary: Close to 300 infrastructure projects deemed not compliant with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)’s evaluation would be removed from the P7.2-trillion proposed national budget…

blocks.text: November 4, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Close to 300 infrastructure projects deemed not compliant with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH)’s evaluation would be removed from the P7.2-trillion proposed national budget for next year, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian vowed yesterday.

“The Senate is committed unequivocally to weeding out unsubstantiated line items, including those lacking concrete and verifiable technical support, to ensure that every item in the final version is shovel-ready. Unverifiable line items will not receive a single peso of public funding,” Gatchalian said, referring to 295 public works projects worth P8.836 billion.

“It’s clear in the Senate’s mandate – no relevant documents, no funds. There should be no room for abuse of people’s money, especially during economic slowdown, when every peso is needed to keep the economy moving,” he said.
At a Senate hearing last September, Gatchalian said more than 62 percent or 7,107 of the total 11,395 infrastructure projects reviewed by his office had at least one major budgetary red flag.
Among the red flags are lacking station numbers and geographical coordinates, overlapping or fragmented projects and conflicting types of work.

After vowing to have the original allocation for Foreign-Assisted Projects in the 2027 budget restored, Senate finance committee chairman JV Ejercito vowed not to tinker with the administration’s “legacy projects.”
MR on SC ruling

Meanwhile, Malacañang said the Office of the Solicitor General is expected to file today a motion for reconsideration on the Supreme Court’s recent ruling declaring as unconstitutional the national budgets for 2024 and 2025 as well as some provisions in the 2026 outlay.

“We have spoken to SolGen (Solicitor General Darlene Marie) Berberabe and tomorrow (Nov. 4), they will file a motion for reconsideration,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said at a briefing yesterday.

The Supreme Court has ruled that the 2024 national budget is unconstitutional because of Congress’ raising the unprogrammed appropriations by P449.5 billion. The high court also struck down last year’s national budget as unconstitutional because of the P17.99-billion increase in the special road fund made by the legislature. — Alexis Romero

articles.title: 5 Filipinos in California charged with illegal voting
articles.summary: Five Filipinos in California were among the 63 people charged in connection with illegal voting, fraudulent voter registration and related election crimes, the United States Department of Justice…

blocks.text: November 4, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Five Filipinos in California were among the 63 people charged in connection with illegal voting, fraudulent voter registration and related election crimes, the United States Department of Justice said Tuesday (Manila time).

The US justice department said the cases include voting by aliens in federal elections, false claims of US citizenship to register or to vote and fraudulent submission of a voter registration application in another state.
“Today’s announcement marks the largest surge of voter-fraud arrests since President Trump returned to office,” said General Todd Blanche.

“These foreign nationals allegedly took advantage of the trust of the American people and flouted the laws that govern our nation’s elections. This Department of Justice will continue investigating and prosecuting voter fraud to restore confidence in our electoral system,” he said.
The identities of the five Filipinos were not revealed.

The foreign nationals charged are lawful permanent residents (LPRs), or green card holders. Although LPRs have legal immigration status in the US, they are not US citizens and are not permitted to vote in US elections.

articles.title: China urged: Walk the talk on peace
articles.summary: If China is indeed serious in its pronouncements that the last thing it wants is war in the region, then it must “walk the talk” and stop making diplomatic provocations over the highly…

blocks.text: November 4, 2026 | 12:00am
West Philippine Sea
Armed Forces of the Philippines

MANILA, Philippines — If China is indeed serious in its pronouncements that the last thing it wants is war in the region, then it must “walk the talk” and stop making diplomatic provocations over the highly sensitive issue of the West Philippine Sea, Mamamayang Liberal party-list Rep. Leila de Lima said.
“China cannot boast of its benevolence while at the same time intimidating and threatening us,” De Lima said yesterday.

“Unless China stops spreading lies and disinformation, puts an end to its baseless claims over the West Philippine Sea and ceases its aggressions against our fishermen, Philippine Coast Guard and Navy personnel, we cannot consider it a negotiator acting in good faith,” the deputy House minority leader said.

De Lima’s remarks echoed a warning raised earlier by House impeachment adviser Robert Ace Barbers that China might portray itself as a “good faith negotiator” during the upcoming Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit in Manila.

“China must walk the talk. Do they (Beijing government) think that, given what they are doing in the WPS and their threats, they can simply make us believe their claims that they are pro-peace and they are our friend?”

De Lima maintained that Beijing cannot present itself as a good-faith negotiator while continuing its aggressive acts in the West Philippine Sea and repeatedly ignoring the July 2016 Arbitral Award that invalidated its vast sea claim.
Barbers said Beijing should act as ASEAN’s “big brother, not a bully” and that it must demonstrate good faith through its actions, not just in its statements.

“The Philippines should at the very least be wary of China potentially appearing as a good faith negotiator, especially if its actions in the West Philippine Sea don’t reflect any good intention,” Barbers said.

“We should not prejudge at this point their intentions but we also shouldn’t ignore their aggressiveness and show of disrespect in our territory and this action seems inconsistent with a commitment to peace in the region,” he said.
He added that the Philippines wants friendship and trade relations with China, but these must be founded on mutual respect.

The Philippines will host the 49th ASEAN Summit on Nov. 16 to 18. China is a regular dialogue partner of the regional bloc and is a participant at several ASEAN-led forums, including the ASEAN-China Summit, ASEAN Plus Three, East Asia Summit and ASEAN Regional Forum.
On Monday, Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr. slammed China’s position to shelve disputes, saying it is not solving the problem.

“China’s position, as stated by its embassy, is to shelve all disputes. That’s not solving the problem. That’s forcing us to accept a status quo where they will use force to have a status quo then ask you to negotiate,” Teodoro said on ANC. — Pia Lee-Brago
